name: Replication Through Removable Media
summary: Adversaries may move onto devices by exploiting or copying malware to devices connected via USB. In the case of Lateral Movement, adversaries may utilize the physical connection of a device to a compromised or malicious charging station or PC to bypass application store requirements and install malicious applications directly. In the case of Initial Access, adversaries may attempt to exploit the device via the connection to gain access to data…

strategies.name: Detection of Replication Through Removable Media

analytics.name: Analytic 1802
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Replication Through Removable Media by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate Application Permission via Android Enterprise DPC / Application Vetting [DevicePolicyManager.getPermissionGrantState(); PackageManager manifest/requested-permission review]; File Creation via Application Vetting / Forensic Acquisition [Dynamic filesystem trace or acquired app-container/filesystem artifacts: File with binary signature (.apk, .dex, .so, .sh) written to app storage or /data/local/tmp/ from USB-mounted path or external storage within $USBInstallWindow$];…

analytics.name: Analytic 1803
analytics.guidance: For iOS, detect Replication Through Removable Media from documented management, network, or vetting evidence; treat state queries as periodic observations rather than real-time events. Correlate Host Status via Apple MDM [DeviceInformation / SecurityInfo / ProfileList / restrictions and compliance queries]; Protected Configuration via Apple MDM [DeviceInformation / SecurityInfo / ProfileList / restrictions and compliance queries]; System Settings via Apple MDM [DeviceInformation / SecurityInfo / ProfileList / restrictions and compliance queries].
